steps: Unpack & pre-fit
Inspect for damage and confirm the hardware kit. Free the firebox from the pallet, lift off the glass frame with the Latch Tool, then set and level it on the four corner bolts (max. 1/2" adjustment).

The log set and optional blower ship separately; don't install them until directed.

Miscellaneous Hardware Kit (packed in the firebox crate)

  • Fuel Conversion Kit, LP
  • Fireplace Conversion Notice Plate
  • Rock Wool Ember Fibers
  • Safety Screen Barrier Guidelines

Pre-installation fit-up

  1. Remove the attachment bracket screws at each side of the base to free the firebox from the pallet.
  2. Take the Latch Tool from the pallet. Pull each spring latch out and up, pivot the top of the glass frame forward and lift it out of the bottom channel.
  3. Set the firebox in its final position and adjust the four corner leveling bolts (max. 1/2" adjustment) to level and plumb it. Front bolts: from inside the firebox, through the side compartments. Rear bolts: tip the firebox forward.
  4. Pull it back out and read the installation requirements before final assembly.
Leveling-bolt adjustment affects the required minimum clearance to combustible top trim and mantel (pp. 8–9). Keep the Latch Tool with the appliance.
Check fireplace & chimney
Clean the flue (a Level II inspection may be needed, NFPA 211), repair damage, and confirm cavity size and clearances. Factory-built: remove doors, screens, grates, damper and ash lip as required.

Approved for a solid fuel-burning factory-built fireplace or a code-approved solid fuel-burning masonry fireplace that meets the minimum cavity (p. 8).

  • Clean the existing flue thoroughly. Depending on its previous use, a Level II inspection may be needed (NFPA 211).
  • Don't install into a chimney that is damaged or contains combustible construction materials; repair first. Clean-outs must be accessible and fit properly.
  • Don't remove bricks or mortar. Masonry or steel may be removed from the smoke shelf and damper frame area for the liners, if that doesn't weaken the structure or reduce protection for combustibles.
  • If the fireplace was modified, fix the metal Fireplace Conversion Notice Plate to the back wall with anchors or masonry nails.
  • Factory-built: remove glass doors, screen rails and mesh, fuel grates, the damper assembly (two 3" liners must pass the damper area) and, if appropriate, the metal ash lip. Keep the parts. Don't cut out sheet metal. A gas access hole of 1 1/2" or less may be drilled in the lower sides or bottom; seal it with noncombustible insulation (p. 12).
This appliance must not be connected to a chimney or flue serving any other appliance.
Run the liners

Pair of listed 3" flexible aluminum liners. Exhaust full length to the cap; intake at least into the first flue tile (U.S.) or full length (required in Canada). Seal the termination kit with high-temperature sealant.

1. Measure the chimney height to the fireplace opening and decide whether both liners run to the top.
  2. Cut both lengths. Label both ends of the exhaust duct to avoid cross-venting.
  3. Attach the duct(s) to the chimney termination kit, drop the liners down from the top and rest the kit on the chimney.
  4. Seal the termination kit to the top of the flue with high-temperature sealant and secure the direct vent cap.
  5. Inside the fireplace, fully extend the ducts and trim so the ends hang approximately 15" from the fireplace floor.

Intake not attached to the termination kit

  • Masonry: the intake flex extends at least into the first flue tile. Factory-built: a minimum 6 foot length into the flue (p. 13).
  • Seal the flue from the room with a block-off plate at the damper area, cut for both liners (noncombustible for masonry, metal for factory-built).
  • A direct vent cap is still required to let fresh air into the flue and the intake.
A high-wind termination cap is recommended for all appliances: M&G Duravent Wind Screen #46DVA-VWG. Prairie-style wind caps are not recommended. Factory-built: don't block off double- or triple-wall chimney air flow.
Connect the vent adaptor

Detach the Vent Adaptor, fix the liners to its marked collars (intake left, exhaust right, facing the unit) with sheet metal screws or clamps, no sealant. Re-engage it with the Latch Tool and refit the lock screw.

1. Remove the lock screw from the Vent Adaptor panel and detach it from the firebox; keep the screws.
  2. Note the exhaust ID on the vent panel. Attach each liner to its collar with sheet metal screws or duct clamps. Sealant is unnecessary.
  3. Position the firebox under the panel and use the Latch Tool to engage it with the pins on the firebox vent manifold.
  4. Reinstall the lock screw.
  5. Push the firebox into its final position (see the order note in the backer plate step).
Intake collar3"
Exhaust collar3" or 4"
3" to 4" OEM collar adaptorsICC TM-I34 · DuraVent 3GVBTI4 P/N 810004525
Backer plates or the cast iron overlay must not block or seal any ventilation openings on a prefabricated fireplace.
Gas connection + leak & pressure test

Min. 3/8" supply to the valve on the left side through the included shut-off; a 36" length of 3/8" flex line is supplied. Leak-test with soapy water; check inlet and manifold pressure with the regulator on HIGH.

• Connection is at the valve on the left side of the unit, facing the front. Supply line: minimum 3/8" diameter, or sized to keep enough pressure at the valve at any input setting.
  • A 36" length of 3/8" flexible gas line is supplied. Where flexible lines aren't permitted, a 3/8" iron nipple and union is recommended.
  • Install the included gas cock in the supply line upstream of the valve (shut-off in the same room). Massachusetts requires a T-handle gas cock (248 CMR). Sediment trap if required by code.
  • Propane: sealant resistant to propane, and an external regulator (p. 2).
  • Leak test: soapy water or a digital gas sensor, never an open flame. Tighten or reconnect any leaking joint and retest.
  • Pressure test: manometer on the valve front, A = inlet, B = manifold, regulator knob on HIGH. Required values: p. 15.
Do not allow inlet pressure to exceed 14.0" WC (or 1/2 PSIG); serious valve damage may result.

This appliance does not require adjustment for altitude.
Fuel conversion (if LP)
Ships for natural gas; LP kit 158119 is included. Swap the burner injector, regulator tower and pilot injector, apply the labels, then leak- and pressure-test, before the surround goes on.

Complete before installing surround plates or placing the insert in the fireplace. To be installed by an authorized Jøtul service technician. Kit 158120 converts back to natural gas.

  1. Turn off the gas supply and disconnect electrical power.
  2. Remove the glass frame with the Latch Tool.
  3. Remove the burner: grasp the two large openings, tilt the front up and pull it forward.
  4. Change the burner injector at the brass fitting at the rear of the firebox (1/2" or 13 mm open-end wrench or deep-well socket). Don't over-tighten; it can damage the brass elbow and cause a leak.
  5. Change the variable regulator tower on the valve (three screws; the original tower, rubber diaphragm and spring come off).
  6. Change the pilot injector, flared end down; orient the head to project flame to the flame sensor and burner ports.
  7. Apply the labels: A, B (on the Rating Plate) and the small valve sticker (on the valve body).
  8. Reinstall the burner: venturi onto the injector, level, front legs on the floor studs.
  9. Leak-check the pilot head and all joints, pressure-test (pp. 14–15), then confirm burner operation (Initial System Check steps 1–3) before final assembly.
Note: the kit contents on p. 16 say Label A is to be completed and applied to the base of the valve compartment; step 7 on p. 16 says to apply it to the right side compartment adjacent to the Rating Plate.
Optional remote or wall thermostat
Remote: receiver on the floor of the housing left of the valve, leads to the valve terminal block. Wall thermostat: 750 millivolt two-wire, min. 16 gauge wire, max. 35 feet.

Remote control kit #224910

  • Contents: receiver/battery box, transmitter, 4 AA receiver batteries, 2 AAA transmitter batteries.
  • Peel the film off the Velcro pad and set the receiver on the floor within the steel housing to the left of the gas control valve (fig. 10.1, #15–16).
  • Connect the receiver leads to the valve terminal block (fig. 7.7).
Note: the manual lists 4 AA receiver and 2 AAA transmitter batteries on p. 18, but its steps on p. 18 put the AAA batteries in the receiver and the AA in the transmitter.
The manual also prints the kit as Remote Control Kit 158103 (p. 18); its accessories list (p. 4) and parts list (p. 33) give #224910.

Wall thermostat

  • Use only a 750 millivolt, DC two-wire circuit wall thermostat.
  • Minimum 16 gauge wire, maximum length 35 feet.
  • Same room as the heater, typically 5 feet off the floor, away from drafts.
  • Remove the Burner Control face plate (upper two #8 hex head screws) and connect each lead to either open terminal block connector on the back of the control panel. Don't overtighten.
The red thermopile wire must be connected to the valve TH/TP terminal to power the thermostat. Label all wires before disconnecting them when servicing the controls.

For either control: burner switch to STAT, then light the pilot.
Firebox panels & log set
Fit any panel kit first, then the chosen log set in order on its pins. Spread the rock wool embers in one even layer; keep the pilot and burner carry-over ports clear.

Panel kits (install before the logs)

Black Reflective Glass#158113
Traditional Red Brick#158114
Black Fluted#158115
  • Panels are very fragile. Handle glass panels with the cotton gloves provided; install them textured side against the firebox walls.
  • Bend the retainer tabs at the upper front corners of the firebox walls out 90° at the perforation. The rear panel rests on the rear burner skirt; the side panels lock it in.
  • Glass kit only: a steel stand-off plate goes on the burner skirt between the wall and each glass side panel.
  • Bend tabs only enough to keep the panels from falling forward.

Log sets

Traditional#158099
Beach Fire#158100
Birch#158275

Install the logs in the order given; each engages pins or notches shown in the photos on pp. 20–25. Use the rock wool fibers from the hardware bag as embers.

Frequently inspect the pilot area and keep it clear of misplaced logs or ember stones. Don't let material obstruct the pilot or burner carry-over ports.
Backer plate, shield & overlay
Hang the backer plate on the outer bracket slots, add the optional Mantle Heat Shield, then hang the surround overlay on the inner slots. Keep the 1/2" air space.

• Complete the gas, vent connection and fuel conversion first. The firebox must sit far enough out of the fireplace to install the backer plate.
  • The backer plate's four hanger hooks engage the outer slots through the back of the firebox brackets (note the small ID hole above each slot). Flange and hooks face out.
  • Choose a backer plate at least 1 inch larger than the fireplace opening. Trimmable plates are for flush-faced fireplaces (p. 8).
  • The optional Mantle Heat Shield #158201 slides over the backer plate.
  • Cast iron and steel overlays ship fully assembled with the integrated safety barrier screen. Their hanger brackets engage the inner slots through the front of the firebox mounting brackets. The cast iron overlay is heavy; get help.
  • Use only the surround options listed on p. 4. Not for use with aftermarket glass doors.
A minimum 1/2" air space must be kept between the overlay and the backer plate or fireplace face. The backer plate hooks maintain it; with no backer plate, fully insert the surround spacer screws on each hanger bracket. Don't modify the hanger brackets or reduce the air space; it may overheat the appliance and void the warranty.
Note: the manual gives two orders for this step. On p. 13 it says to push the insert fully into its final position and not to install the backer plate until all other assembly and system checks are done; on p. 26 it says not to place the insert in its final position until the backer plate is installed.
Initial system check
Purge the line, light the pilot and check the three pilot flames; burner switch ON; correct the flame picture at the air shutter if needed. Brief the homeowner and leave the manual.

1. Purge: open the gas supply valve. On first lighting, or after a long period of unuse, it takes a few moments to clear air from the line.
  2. Pilot: light it per the rating plate and the lighting instructions (p. 37). All three pilot flames project out of the hood, blueish-yellow, extending approximately 1" to the burner ports, thermopile and thermocouple; strong and steady, not fluttering or lifting; fully engulfing the upper 1/4" of the thermocouple and thermopile. Adjust with the pilot screw on the valve body (fig. 7.2), qualified gas technician only.
  3. Burner: burner switch ON. In a cold flue the pilot may need 10–15 minutes to establish draft first. The regulator knob sets fire intensity.
  4. STAT: for optional remote or wall thermostat control.

Flame picture / air shutter (p. 29)

Primary air shutter under the firebox at the center of the valve compartment; factory setting 1/2 open. Adjust in 1/8" – 1/4" increments and wait a few minutes between changes. Loosen the wing nut; push the handle in to decrease air, pull it out to increase; tighten the lock nut. Propane generally needs a less restricted setting than natural gas. No smoke or soot should be evident; check log placement first.

Give the manual to the homeowner and show them basic operation before leaving (p. 3).

panels.title: Insufficient gas pressure
items: Small pilot flame → poor pilot rectification and/or frequent burner outages
Little variation in flame picture between HI and LO
Not enough gas for more than one appliance → nuisance outages or gas surges

panels.title: Excessive gas pressure
items: Permanent valve damage → complete appliance shutdown
Pilot flame too large → flame sensor overheats and shuts down
Sooting from impingement and/or incorrect fuel-to-air mix

panels.title: Flame picture / air shutter
items: Too little air → very long yellow flames and soot on logs, firebox walls, termination cap
Too much air → very blue, transparent or weak "anemic" flames
Soot or smoke → confirm log placement first, then open the shutter for more air

panels.title: Pilot won't stay lit
items: Goes out after the knob is released → repeat lighting steps 5–8
Knob doesn't spring back → stop and immediately call a service technician or gas supplier
Won't stay lit after several tries → knob to OFF; call a technician or gas supplier

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
The pilot is lit by hand. Before lighting, smell all around the fireplace for gas, next to the floor too. If you smell any, stop and see Safety.

  1. Read the safety information.
  2. Get to the lower controls.
  3. Turn the ON/OFF switch to OFF, or the thermostat (if used) to its lowest setting.
  4. Make sure the gas supply shut-off valve is open.
  5. Push the gas control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF.
  6. Wait five minutes to clear out any gas. If you then smell gas, stop.
  7. Push the knob in slightly and turn it counterclockwise to PILOT.
  8. Push the knob all the way in and hold it. Press the red button repeatedly until the pilot lights. Keep holding about one minute, then let go. The knob should spring back and the pilot stay lit. If it goes out, repeat steps 5 to 8.
  9. Turn the knob counterclockwise to ON.
  10. Turn the ON/OFF switch to ON, or set the thermostat.
Use only your hand. Push in or turn the gas control knob by hand only, and never use tools. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
If the knob doesn't spring back when you let go, stop and immediately call your service technician or gas supplier. If the pilot won't stay lit after several tries, turn the knob to OFF and call your service technician or gas supplier.
Note: on MV models the pilot shuts off after seven days without a call for heat. On p. 28 the manual says it then re-ignites automatically at the next call for heat; on p. 30 and p. 37 it says to relight it by hand.

off.title: Turning it off
off.html:
Everyday: burner off, pilot on

Turn the ON/OFF switch to OFF. The flames go out and the pilot stays lit. Leaving the pilot on through the heating season also keeps foggy glass to a minimum.

Complete shutdown

  1. Turn the ON/OFF switch to OFF.
  2. Get to the lower controls.
  3. Push the gas control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF. Don't force it.

After a complete shutdown, use the full lighting steps to start it again.

It stays hot. Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch the glass until it has cooled, and never let children touch it. On a thermostat, the fireplace may be very hot even when the burner doesn't seem to be on.

MV models: if there's no call for heat for seven days, the pilot shuts itself off. See Lighting.

firstfire.title: Your first fires
firstfire.html:
The paint on your insert cures with heat during the first firings. That gives off an odor and some visible smoke. It's temporary.

Before the very first fire

  • Ventilate: open doors and windows, and use a fan to move fresh air through the room.
  • Vacate: the fumes are non-toxic, but they can bother babies, small children, pregnant women, older people, pets and anyone with breathing difficulties.

The break-in routine

Once your installer has checked the burner at all heat levels, run the fireplace on a low setting for 2–4 hours, then on a high setting for 2–4 hours. The first time, or in a cold flue, the pilot may need to burn 10–15 minutes before the burner will light.

Then clean the glass

Curing paint and log-set material can leave a white, powdery film on the inside of the glass. Clean it off after the first few fires with a non-abrasive household glass cleaner or warm water. Left on, it can etch the glass permanently.

Don't use ammonia-based cleaners.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Condensation on the glass is normal with gas fireplaces, and a film of particles can build up on the inside.

  1. Wait until the glass is cool. Never clean it hot.
  2. Wipe it with a dampened, soft cloth.
  3. Polish it with a dry, soft towel.

A specially formulated ceramic glass cleaner is fine too. After the first few fires, also clean off the white curing film so it can't etch the glass.

Never use abrasive or ammonia-based cleaners, and take care not to scratch the surface. Scratches weaken the glass. If you see any, have the panel replaced, with Jøtul part 158135 only.

Handle with care

  • The glass can shatter if something strikes it. Don't slam or strike it.
  • Never run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken.
  • Glass replacement should be done by a licensed or qualified service person.

remote.title: Remote control & wall thermostat
remote.html:
A remote control and a wall thermostat are both options. Either one works the same way:

  1. Set the fireplace burner switch to STAT.
  2. Light the pilot (see Lighting).
  3. With the pilot lit, the burner responds to calls for heat from the thermostat or the remote.

For buttons and features, follow the instructions that come with your remote or thermostat.

A wall thermostat goes in the same room as the fireplace, typically 5 feet off the floor, away from drafts.
It can come on by itself. On a thermostat, the fireplace may be very hot even when the burner doesn't seem to be running. Keep children away, and keep the remote where they can't reach it.
Note: the remote kit comes with 4 AA and 2 AAA batteries. The kit list on p. 18 puts the AA batteries in the receiver and the AAA batteries in the transmitter; the steps on p. 18 put the AAA batteries in the receiver and the AA batteries in the transmitter.

MV models: the pilot shuts off after seven days with no call for heat. See Lighting for how it comes back.

sounds.title: Sounds and fog: what's normal
sounds.html:
A soft woof or thud

A muffled "woof" or "thud" when the burner lights and goes out is normal. If it gets unusually loud or disturbing, stop using the fireplace and call a qualified service technician.

Creaks and pings

Cast iron and steel expand and contract as the temperature changes. The creaking and pinging is natural thermal movement.

A low hum

The optional blower hums slightly on its low setting, and gets louder as the fan speeds up.

Fog on the glass

Condensation forms on the glass each time the burner lights from a cold start. It clears as the glass heats up. Leaving the pilot on during the heating season keeps it to a minimum.

Not normal: smoke or soot once the first few hours of paint curing are over. Check that the logs are placed correctly. If it continues, the air shutter needs adjusting, which only a qualified service technician should do.

blower.title: Using the blower
blower.html:
The blower is optional. If your fireplace has one, use the switch and speed knob on its switch panel.

Manual

The blower runs whatever the firebox temperature, and stays on whether or not the burner is lit, until you switch it to Auto or Off. The knob sets the speed.

Auto

The blower turns on when its thermostat (a snapstat) reaches 140°F (60°C). When the burner shuts off, it keeps running until the firebox cools below 140°F.

Note: p. 30 says the blower keeps running after the burner shuts off until the firebox cools below 140°F; the parts list on p. 33 names the snapstat "140-120 deg° F".

Power

  • The blower needs 120 VAC power.
  • Plug its three-prong plug directly into a properly grounded three-prong outlet. Never cut or remove the grounding prong.
  • Always disconnect the power before any service on the fireplace.

safety.title: Safety around the fireplace
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Put out any open flame and open windows.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone, and follow their instructions.
  • If you can't reach your gas supplier, call the fire department.

These steps are printed on the cover and on the lighting page (p. 37).

Everyday safety

  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • The safety screen must stay installed. If it gets damaged, replace it only with Jøtul Screen Barrier part 226317. Put back any screen, glass or guard removed for service before using the fireplace.
  • Supervise young children in the room. If anyone at risk lives with you, a child guard or safety gate is recommended.
  • Keep clothing and anything flammable away. Never store or use gasoline or other flammable liquids nearby.
  • Use only natural gas or propane. Never burn wood, paper, cardboard or coal in it.
  • Don't use the fireplace if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the fireplace and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
In Massachusetts, a carbon monoxide detector must be installed in the same room as the fireplace.

care.title: Cleaning & yearly service
care.html:
Have a qualified service technician inspect the fireplace and its venting system before use and at least once a year.

Cleaning (burner and firebox cold)

  • Monthly: vacuum the controls area under the firebox, more often if pet hair is around.
  • At least yearly: vacuum the firebox, more often with pets. A flexible attachment reaches the valve compartment and blower area. Use a soft brush attachment on the logs.
  • Clear any debris from the burner ports, especially the pilot carry-over ports.

Checks

  • Look over the pilot assembly for corrosion. Have damaged parts replaced by a qualified service technician.
  • Inspect the glass gasket every year for wear or stiffness, and make sure it still seals. The seal keeps combustion gases out of the room. Replace it if necessary.
Keep the area around the fireplace clear of combustible materials, gasoline and other flammable liquids. Always disconnect electrical power before servicing.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Jøtul's limited warranty covers the original retail purchaser, from the date of purchase. It isn't transferable.

Cast iron, steel doors, surround components, firebox5 years
Burner, burner treatments, firebox panels2 years
Enamel finish (peeling or fading)2 years
Gas & electrical components (controls, plumbing, valve, blower)1 year

Making a claim

Keep your dated sales receipt. Contact your nearest authorized Jøtul dealer, who processes the claim. Jøtul must receive notice of a possible defect within 60 days of when it was first discovered.

Not covered, for example

  • Normal wear parts: paint, gaskets and glass (unless damaged by thermal stress)
  • Installation that doesn't follow the manual or fire and building codes
  • Unauthorized modification, use or repair
  • Enamel damage from misuse, such as bubbling, cracking or discoloration
  • Travel time, loss of service, and damage in transit
The warranty is void if installation or service is done by someone other than an authorized installer, service agency or gas supplier. This is a summary; the full terms are in the manual.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas5.0 – 7.0 in. WC
Propane11.0 – 14.0 in. WC

Measure with a manometer at test point A on the front of the valve, regulator set to its highest setting. Propane needs an external regulator (p. 2). Supply line: minimum 3/8", or sized to keep enough pressure at the valve at any input setting (p. 14).

Do not allow inlet pressure to exceed 14.0" WC (or 1/2 PSIG); serious valve damage may result.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas1.1 – 3.8 in. WC
Propane2.9 – 11.0 in. WC

Test point B on the valve front, regulator set to its highest setting. Outside this band, expect the symptoms under "Gas pressure & flame faults".

Pilot flame check (p. 28)

All three pilot flames project out of the hood, blueish-yellow, approximately 1" over to the burner ports, thermopile and thermocouple; strong and steady, fully engulfing the upper 1/4" of the thermocouple and thermopile. Adjust with the pilot screw on the valve body (fig. 7.2), qualified gas technician only.

specFirebox.title: Minimum fireplace cavity
specFirebox.html:
A · Inside height20"
B · Inside width20" (at 14 1/2" depth)

For a solid fuel-burning factory-built fireplace or a code-approved solid fuel-burning masonry fireplace. Don't modify the insert to make it fit.

Covering the opening

  • Cast iron overlay: covers a maximum fireplace opening of 22" high × 35" wide, with a 1/4" face overlap.
  • Backer plate: choose one at least 1 inch larger than the opening. 3-sided: 40"W × 26"H (#158106), 41"W × 28"H (#158107), 42"W × 30"H (#158108). Trimmable 46"W × 34"H: 3-sided #158109, 4-sided #158110 (for flush-faced fireplaces).

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Vent through the chimney with a pair of 3" flexible aluminum liners listed for gas appliances: exhaust from the port on top of the unit, intake to the air intake port.

Termination cap above unitmin. 10 ft · max. 35 ft
Liner diameter3"; LP runs over 10 ft: 4" exhaust recommended, with a 3" intake run to the terminus
Horizontal runsnot permitted
Liner ends in fireplaceapproximately 15" from the floor
  • Exhaust runs the full length of the chimney, directly to the termination cap. Intake: through the damper and at least into the first flue tile (U.S. only), or full length. In Canada both must run full length.
  • If the intake doesn't run full length, a block-off plate must be installed above the unit, below the end of the intake duct (normally at the damper).
  • Label the exhaust duct at both ends to avoid cross-venting.
  • Never connect to a chimney or flue serving any other appliance. Liners may not be exposed to any living space.
  • Use listed 3" or 4" flexible vent parts from one approved manufacturer only (list on p. 34); don't mix manufacturers.

Gas Vent Rule (minimum height from roof)

Flat to 6/121'0"
Over 7/12 to 9/122'0"
Over 10/12 to 12/124'0"
Over 13/12 to 16/126'0"
Over 17/12 to 21/128'0"
Steep roofs, nearby trees or wind can cause weak draft or downdrafts; a taller vent or a high-wind cap may help. A high-wind cap is recommended for all appliances.
Using an existing chimney as the air intake isn't covered by the product certification. Consult the code authority having jurisdiction first.

conflicts.issue: GI 545 DV MV pilot after the seven-day no-call-for-heat shut-off: p. 28 says it automatically re-ignites at the next call for heat; p. 30 (pilot limit note) and p. 37 (lighting step 11) say it must be relit by hand. Also noted in the remote drawer.

Remote kit batteries: the contents list gives 4 AA receiver and 2 AAA transmitter batteries, but steps 1-2 say to insert the AAA batteries in the receiver and the AA batteries in the transmitter. Also noted in step6.
Remote control kit part number: 'Remote Control Kit 158103' in section 7.4.1 vs 'Remote Control #224910' in the accessories list and '224910 Remote Control Kit' in the parts list.

Backer plate sequence: p. 13 says push the insert fully into its final position and do not install the backer plate until all other assembly and system checks are completed; p. 26 says do not place the insert in its final position until the backer plate is installed.
Blower Auto shut-off: operation text says the blower runs until the firebox cools below 140°F; the parts list names the snapstat '140-120 deg° F'.
Conversion Label A location: kit contents say apply to the base of the valve compartment; procedure step 7 says apply to the right side compartment adjacent to the Rating Plate.

review.notes: The manual covers both the GI 545 DV and the GI 545 DV MV (cover: 'For Stoves S/N >58001458'); the guide covers both and calls out MV differences (P.4.1 efficiency, SIT 821 valve, seven-day pilot shut-off). Catalog check: BTU inputs, 3" liners, optional blower and mobile-home approval match; catalog efficiency 61.37/64.26 matches the GI 545 DV, while the DV MV is 63.28/65.39 (pp. 2, 4). Unit dimensions (19.75 x 29.625 x 14.5 in), weight (163 lb) and heating area (1,800 sq ft) are not in the manual text, so they could not be checked; unit dimensions appear only in the fig. 5.1 drawing (p. 7). Lighting page p. 37 is two-column and the extracted text interleaves steps 5 and 9; the raw page text confirms step 5 = clockwise to OFF and step 9 = counterclockwise to ON. Decoded with the 29-code-point rule: the end of the wiring caution on p. 18 ('...OPERATION. ALWAYS VERIFY PROPER OPERATION AFTER SERVICING THE APPLIANCE.') and the scrambled page headers on pp. 14 and 18. Not decodable and not used: the p. 14 heading above the assembly list and a p. 18 figure label. Metric misprints (guide uses inches only): hearth width 3 1/8" is (10.5 cm) in the section 5.3 text but (8 cm) in the fig. 5.3 legend (p. 8); mantel 39 3/4" is printed '(1010 cm)' (p. 9). Hearth protection text on p. 8 names only the GI 545 DV MV; the 12" depth is measured from the facing material in the text and from the opening in the legend (both shown). The 'Minimum Ceiling Height from Hearth Surface: 64 3/4"' appears in the fig. 5.6 (with-shield) block; shown there. Internal page references and the table of contents are out of date (e.g., 'Initial System Check on page 26' is physical p. 28; approved vents 'page 32' is p. 34; parts list 'pages 31' is p. 33; fig. 10.1 'page 30' is p. 32). Log placement is shown only in photos (pp. 20-25) and is not transcribed. Naming inconsistencies there: Traditional set list says #7 Left Small / #8 Right Small but figs. 7.18-7.19 say Small Right #7 / Small Left #8; Beach Fire list says rock #5 Right Skirt but fig. 7.32 says 'left Skirt Rock #5'. The Birch Log Set 158275 (section 7.8) is not in the p. 4 accessories list. Backer plate/overlay slot letters (B/C/D) disagree between text and figure on pp. 26-27; letters not used. Fig. 8.3 air-shutter labels (OPEN/CLOSE, decrease/increase air) are ambiguous in the extraction; guide uses the body text (push in = decrease air, pull out = increase). The pressure-fault list (p. 15) and pilot-orifice step (p. 16) say 'flame sensor' and 'pilot rectification' although p. 28 describes a thermocouple and thermopile; transcribed as printed. The p. 16 minimum-input table prints its 2000-4000 ft row as placeholders ('00000'); p. 14 says no altitude adjustment is required and p. 4 lists orifices for 0-4500 ft. The p. 14 assembly list includes 'Optional Blower' but the manual gives no blower installation procedure (operation only, p. 30). Remote button functions are in the kit's own instructions, not this manual. High-altitude standard is written CAN/CGA 2.17-M17 on the cover and CAN/CSA 2.17-2017 on p. 4. Massachusetts CO detector text on p. 2 cites NFPA 720 2005 and 2002 editions; not used. The 'what to do if you smell gas' block is in English (cover and p. 37); no translation needed.
